title: Andreev Scattering Driven Surface Photogalvanic Effect
authors: V. M. Kovalev, I. G. Savenko
abstract: The surface photogalvanic effect is a powerful tool for generating macroscopic direct currents in centrosymmetric film structures via asymmetric scattering of carriers at film boundaries. Here, we uncover a fundamentally distinct regime of photoinduced transport in normal metal-superconductor heterostructures, in which the macroscopic photocurrent is governed by Andreev scattering at the interface rather than by classical scattering. We demonstrate that the interplay between asymmetric surface scattering and Andreev retroreflection yields a giant, strongly frequency-dependent anomalous photocurrent. Strikingly, the electron-hole conversion at the normal-superconducting interface dictates a macroscopic sign reversal of the photogalvanic current across the superconducting transition, and induces non-analytic spectral kinks exactly at the pairing gap frequency. Our results establish the Andreev reflection-driven surface photogalvanic effect as a platform for optical control of superconducting correlations and suggest a direct, non-invasive spectroscopic probe for gap dynamics in hybrid quantum devices.
summary: This theoretical work establishes a microscopic theory for the Surface Photogalvanic Effect in normal metal/superconductor junctions. It shows that the photocurrent is dominated by Andreev scattering, leading to unique signatures like a sign reversal and sharp spectral kinks at the superconducting gap edge. This positions the effect as a powerful tool for optically probing superconducting properties.
main_problem: The paper investigates how Andreev scattering at a normal metal-superconductor (NS) interface fundamentally alters the macroscopic photogalvanic current compared to classical scattering mechanisms.
main_result: The Andreev scattering-driven SPGE yields a giant, strongly frequency-dependent photocurrent exhibiting a sign reversal across the superconducting transition and displaying non-analytic kinks at the pairing gap frequency.
method: The authors developed a microscopic kinetic theory approach, solving a linearized kinetic equation for the non-equilibrium electron distribution function by incorporating boundary conditions derived from the BTK formalism.
model_or_system: The system modeled is a normal metal (N) film deposited on a Superconducting (SC) substrate (NS heterostructure), analyzed in various geometries (3D, 2D lateral strips). The theory unifies classical surface scattering with coherent Andreev charge transfer.
key_observables: Macroscopic direct SPGE current density ($j_x$ or $\chi$), which is sensitive to the photon frequency ($\omega$) and the superconducting gap ($\Delta$).
important_parameters: Superconducting gap ($\Delta$), interface barrier strength ($Z$), film thickness ($d$), and incident photon frequency ($\omega$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the photoinduced correction is odd in momentum and utilizes the dipole approximation for calculating the electron-photon collision integral source term ($G_k$).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic setup (oblique incidence, lateral 2D geometry) and show the normalized photocurrent ($\chi$) dependence on the reduced frequency ($\omega/\Delta$) for different boundary conditions.
paper_structure: The paper builds from developing the general kinetic equation for the SPGE in NS heterostructures, deriving the necessary boundary conditions (including Andreev reflection), and then analyzing the resulting current in various limits (thin-film, 2D, etc.) to highlight the unique quantum signatures.
why_interesting: The strong dependence on the superconducting gap and the emergence of non-analytic features provide a direct, non-invasive spectroscopic probe for gap dynamics, linking optical measurements to superconducting correlations.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic of the normal-metal–superconductor (NS) heterostructure. (a) A normal-metal film deposited on a SC substrate is illuminated by obliquely incident electromagnetic radiation. (b) Corresponding energy-band diagram illustrating the microscopic subgap transport mechanisms. Photoexcited nonequilibrium electrons experience specular scattering at the upper film-vacuum boundary, while coherent charge transfer at the NS interface is dictated by the continuous competition between normal specular reflection (electron-to-electron) and Andreev retroreflection (electron-to-hole).

FIG. 2. Normalized surface photogalvanic photocurrent co- efficient χ (in arbitrary units) as a function of the reduced frequency ω/∆for an ideal NS interface (Z = 0). Curves correspond to different values of the specularity parameter D at the film-vacuum boundary (D = 0, 0.5, 0.8, 1.0). In the subgap regime (ω/∆< 1), all curves collapse onto a single line due to unit Andreev reflection probability (A = 1).

FIG. 3. Normalized surface photogalvanic current coefficient χ and its frequency derivative dχ/dω (in arbitrary units) as functions of the reduced frequency ω/∆for finite barrier strengths at the NS interface. The top row shows the photocurrent for (a) Z = 0.5 and (b) Z = 0.7. The bottom row (c, d) shows the corresponding derivatives. Curves denote different values of the film-vacuum specularity parameter D (D = 0, 0.8, 0.9, 1.0). Red and green dots show the points of electric current sign reversal.

FIG. 4. Schematic of the lateral 2D geometry for the surface photogalvanic effect. A purely 2D normal-metal strip of width d is laterally coupled to a semi-infinite SC region. The sys- tem is uniformly illuminated by normally incident electromag- netic radiation, with the light’s polarization plane oriented at an oblique angle to the NS interface. Unlike the quasi-3D thick-film regime, this lateral configuration ensures that the macroscopic photoresponse retains its direct dependence on the quantum Andreev scattering processes regardless of the total strip width.
